data.name: Emerald City Confidential™
data.detailed_description:
<p>Work with the world's most cunning detective in the shadowy underbelly of the Emerald City of Oz! As Petra, you'll be lured deep into mysteries involving new foes and familiar faces; Scarecrow, Lion, and Toto included. This is Oz as you've never seen it before! Solve your detective's quest and unravel a conspiracy of magic and intrigue! Follow a case through five chapters full of puzzles, witnesses, suspects, and allies.</p>
<ul>
<li>Over 50 beautiful and detailed environments to explore
<li>First PlayFirst game with full voiceover — 36 characters and over 6,000 lines of spoken dialog
<li>A new story and twist on the timeless world and classic characters of Oz
</ul>

reviews.review:
Emerald City Confidential takes the colorful mythology of Oz and transforms it into a surprisingly effective detective mystery filled with corruption, secrets, political intrigue, and magical conspiracies. Developed by Wadjet Eye Games and published by Electronic Arts, it is a traditional point-and-click adventure built around investigation, dialogue, exploration, and puzzle solving. Instead of attempting to recreate the cheerful tone normally associated with Oz, the game imagines a more complicated version of the setting where familiar characters have moved on with their lives and the Emerald City has developed problems considerably darker than wicked witches and yellow brick roads.

The player assumes the role of Petra, a private investigator whose latest case gradually becomes far more dangerous and important than expected. What begins as detective work develops into a broader mystery involving powerful individuals and hidden agendas. Petra is a fitting protagonist for this interpretation of Oz because she approaches its magical absurdities with the attitude of a hardened investigator. Her personality gives the adventure a noir flavor without turning the entire experience into a grim drama. Humor, fantasy, mystery, and occasional darker themes coexist throughout the story.

One of the strongest aspects is how naturally recognizable Oz characters and locations are incorporated into the mystery. Scarecrow, Lion, Toto, and other familiar personalities are not included merely as nostalgic references. They have places within the game's society and often differ from the uncomplicated versions players may expect. This creates the impression that Oz has continued evolving beyond the famous adventures associated with it. Even players without extensive knowledge of the original stories can follow the plot, while those familiar with Oz mythology have additional details and reinterpretations to appreciate.

Gameplay remains firmly rooted in classic adventure-game design. Petra travels between locations, examines objects, questions characters, collects useful items, and determines how clues or inventory objects can solve problems blocking her investigation. There is little emphasis on reflexes or mechanical skill. Progress instead depends upon observation, conversations, logical associations, and occasional experimentation. The interface is straightforward enough that players unfamiliar with older point-and-click adventures should be able to understand the basic mechanics quickly.

The puzzles generally prioritize narrative momentum rather than extreme difficulty. Many solutions are logical within the context of the environment or information obtained through conversations. Experienced adventure players may consider some challenges relatively easy, but this accessibility also prevents the mystery from becoming buried beneath unnecessarily obscure puzzle logic. There are still moments where players may need to revisit locations, reconsider available items, or pay closer attention to dialogue, but the overall progression tends to remain approachable.

Its substantial amount of dialogue is particularly important because investigating characters forms such a large part of the experience. The game includes dozens of voiced personalities and thousands of spoken lines, helping the cast feel more substantial than simple puzzle dispensers. Questioning people frequently provides clues while simultaneously revealing details about the unusual society surrounding Petra. The voice performances also complement the noir-inspired writing and make extended conversations more engaging.

Visually, Emerald City Confidential uses illustrated 2D environments that suit its unusual combination of fantasy and detective fiction. The numerous locations provide enough variety to make investigating Oz consistently interesting. Bright fantasy imagery remains present, but many areas carry a moodier atmosphere appropriate for a mystery involving questionable characters and dangerous secrets. Character animation and certain interface elements inevitably show their age, yet the stylized artwork has retained more personality than a technically ambitious but visually generic presentation might have.

The five-chapter structure gives the story a steady rhythm and allows the investigation to expand naturally. Each stage introduces new information and complications while pushing Petra deeper into the central conspiracy. The adventure is largely linear, however, so players should not expect a detective simulation where suspects can be pursued in radically different orders or where deductions produce numerous branching outcomes. The pleasure comes from uncovering a carefully constructed story rather than creating a completely personalized investigation.

Its limitations mostly stem from that traditional structure. Players wanting action, open-ended exploration, elaborate character progression, or exceptionally difficult puzzles will probably find the mechanics too restrained. Some interactions can also feel dated when compared with modern narrative adventures. However, these weaknesses matter considerably less for players who value dialogue, atmosphere, imaginative world-building, and a focused mystery.

Steam Deck compatibility is less straightforward than with games carrying an official Valve Verified designation. Emerald City Confidential have an official Steam Deck compatibility rating of Playable. As an older Windows-focused point-and-click title, it should therefore be treated as unofficial or potentially requiring manual adjustments rather than assumed to be fully supported. The mouse-oriented interface may also make trackpad input preferable to conventional controller controls. Players specifically purchasing it for Steam Deck should expect possible compatibility or configuration issues.

Ultimately, Emerald City Confidential succeeds because it does more than attach detective mechanics to a famous fantasy setting. It builds a convincing alternate interpretation of Oz and gives players a protagonist whose investigative role provides an excellent excuse to uncover its hidden problems. The combination of noir storytelling, recognizable mythology, extensive conversations, accessible puzzles, and illustrated environments gives the adventure a character that remains distinctive despite its age. It is especially worthwhile for players who enjoy classic point-and-click mysteries and imaginative reinterpretations of familiar fictional worlds.

Rating: 8/10
